{{Short description|Inequality relating the primorial to square of the next prime number}}
In [[number theory]], '''Bonse's inequality''', named after H.&nbsp;Bonse,<ref>{{cite journal |first=H. |last=Bonse |title=Über eine bekannte Eigenschaft der Zahl 30 und ihre Verallgemeinerung |journal=Archiv der Mathematik und Physik |volume=3 |issue=12 |year=1907 |pages=292&ndash;295 }}</ref> relates the size of a [[primorial]] to the smallest prime that does not appear in its [[prime factorization]]. It states that for all <math>n\geq 4</math>, if <math>p_1,\dots,p_n,p_{n+1}</math> are the first <math>n+1</math> [[prime number]]s, then

: <math> p_n\# = \prod_{i=1}^n p_i > p_{n+1}^2. </math>

Barkley Rosser showed an upper bound where <math>n\#\leq 2.83^n</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rosser |first=Barkley |date=January 1941 |title=Explicit Bounds for Some Functions of Prime Numbers |url=https://doi.org/10.2307/2371291 |journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=63 |issue=1 |pages=211-232 |doi=10.2307/2371291|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
